record.original_question: For the hard-core lattice gas (independent-set model) on a countably infinite graph G=(V,E) of maximum degree Delta, with vertex fugacities {w_x} and Gibbs measures defined for nonnegative fugacities, is it true that uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure holds whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon)*(Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta for all vertices x and some epsilon>0 (possibly even epsilon=0)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 For any countably infinite graph G of maximum degree Delta, the hard-core lattice gas on G has a unique Gibbs measure whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon) x (Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta ... for all vertices x, for some epsilon > 0. [Perhaps this is true even with epsilon = 0.]

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a countably infinite graph of maximum degree $\Delta\ge 3$. The hard-core lattice gas on $G$ with vertex fugacities $\{w_x\}_{x\in V}$, $w_x\ge 0$, is the family of probability measures on $\{0,1\}^V$ (interpreted as independent sets, where $\sigma_x=1$ means $x$ is occupied) defined by the Gibbsian specifications: for each finite $\Lambda\subset V$ and each boundary condition $\eta\in\{0,1\}^{V\setminus\Lambda}$ that is compatible with the hard-core constraint (no two adjacent vertices are both occupied),
$$\mu_\Lambda^\eta(\sigma_\Lambda)=\frac{1}{Z_\Lambda^\eta}\,\mathbf{1}\{\sigma_\Lambda\cup\eta\text{ is an independent set}\}\prod_{x\in\Lambda:\sigma_x=1}w_x.$$
A probability measure $\mu$ on $\{0,1\}^V$ is an (infinite-volume) Gibbs measure if its conditional distributions agree with these specifications. Let
$$\lambda_c(\Delta):=\frac{(\Delta-1)^{\Delta-1}}{(\Delta-2)^\Delta}$$
denote the uniqueness threshold of the hard-core model on the infinite $\Delta$-regular tree.

Prove or disprove: For every countably infinite graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta$, the hard-core lattice gas on $G$ has a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure whenever there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$$0\le w_x\le (1-\varepsilon)\,\lambda_c(\Delta)\qquad\text{for all }x\in V.$$
Determine also whether the statement remains true with $\varepsilon=0$.
artifact.category_tag: hard-core lattice gas / Gibbs measure uniqueness
artifact.status_search_result: The related conjecture of Sokal concerning zero-freeness of the independence polynomial in a complex neighborhood of $[0,\lambda_c(\Delta))$ for all graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ was resolved by Peters and Regts (2017), yielding deterministic FPTAS up to the tree threshold. However, the question of uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure on all countably infinite graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ up to the tree uniqueness threshold $\lambda_c(\Delta)$ appears to remain open in general; uniqueness up to this threshold is known on the $\Delta$-regular tree and (via correlation decay/strong spatial mixing arguments) implies results for amenable graphs in specific settings, but a full proof for arbitrary infinite graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ has not been established. Related questions (e.g., whether strong spatial mixing on the tree transfers to all bounded-degree graphs) are explicitly open.

status_evidence.title: On a conjecture of Sokal concerning roots of the independence polynomial
status_evidence.snippet: Peters and Regts prove Sokal's conjecture: independence polynomial has no zeros in a complex neighborhood of [0, lambda_c(Delta)) for all graphs of maximum degree Delta.
status_evidence.claim: Zero-freeness version (Sokal's conjecture) resolved; implies algorithmic uniqueness-type statements up to the tree threshold.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness thresholds on trees versus graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses conjectures relating tree uniqueness thresholds to general bounded-degree graphs for the hard-core model.
status_evidence.claim: The transfer of uniqueness from the tree to all bounded-degree graphs is discussed as a conjectural program.

status_evidence.title: The hard-core model in graph theory
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the hard-core model and uniqueness/zero-freeness thresholds on bounded-degree graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey indicates Gibbs-measure uniqueness on general infinite graphs at the tree threshold is not fully resolved.
